source_text: “There is often a great deal of difference between the will of all and the general will; the latter takes account only of the common interest, while the former takes private interest into account, and is no more than a sum of particular wills.”

model_response: Rousseau argues that the general will is different from the will of all, because the will of all only adds up what each person privately wants, while the general will looks at the common interest. This means a majority isn't automatically right: a community has to ask what is good for everyone, not just what most people want.
